channel.title: Robotics Directory - Commercial Robots
channel.description: Browse 1412 commercial robots in the Robotics Directory. Specs, prices, images and comparison.

item.title: FarmDroid FD60
item.description: FD60 is FarmDroid’s larger battery-driven seeding and mechanical-weeding platform,introduced in autumn 2026 with customer deliveries planned from January 2027. It supports up to 20 rows and 6.75 m working width,using the 14 mm seeding system and stored RTK GPS seed coordinates. Solar charging is supplemented by a petrol generator that recharges the battery. It does not support the FD20 +Spray option. Daily and seasonal area targets are planning claims; orders do not prove delivered units.

item.title: Upside Robotics Maize Runner
item.description: Maize Runner is a solar-powered autonomous robot from Waterloo, Ontario startup Upside Robotics that applies precisely dosed liquid fertilizer between 30-inch corn rows, using onboard sensors to time applications and cut nitrogen use by up to 70%. It is 22 inches wide, carries a 50-liter tank, runs about 10 hours per charge with a 60-minute solar recharge at its base station, and covers roughly 1 acre per hour. The company announced a $7.5 million seed round in February 2026 and was operating across about 3,000 corn acres in Ontario, Canada.

item.title: Locus Robotics Locus Array
item.description: Locus Array is Locus Robotics’ mobile manipulation system for in-aisle picking, transport and order consolidation. The manufacturer announced its global launch on April 13, 2026 with early-access North American deployments and planned regional scaling. NeuraGrasp handles selected soft, porous and unpackaged items; continuous operation and mixed-fleet SKU coverage do not establish single-battery endurance, gripper load or universal item success.

item.title: SMP Robotics Systems Corp. Argus S5.4
item.description: Argus S5.4 is the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX mobile AI/security platform announced March 2, 2026, with shipments stated to begin in March 2026. It supports accredited third-party developers and certified onboard software distributed through SMP Store. The announcement does not establish exact mass, dimensions, battery endurance, camera package, IP rating or current stock; S5.3 and historical S5.2 values are not transferred.

item.title: Greenfield Robotics BOTONY
item.description: BOTONY is Greenfield Robotics' autonomous agricultural robot for chemical-free mechanical weed control in broadacre crops such as soybeans, milo, cotton and corn. The manufacturer offers wheeled and tracked configurations and estimates approximately 7 acres per day per robot under optimal conditions. Cutting is optimally initiated when weeds reach 3–5 inches, with a specified 60-inch turn zone. Each robot uses the GreenTRIP RTK system for field mapping and autonomous navigation with a 15 km range radius and centimeter-level accuracy, onboard cameras with human-detection algorithms and geofencing, and the Operator software for remote monitoring and intervention. The company reports a 2025 leased fleet of 23 robots in seven states and 70 orders for 2026 delivery, and operates made-to-order without maintaining robot inventory.

item.title: Lucid Gravity Robotaxi
item.description: The Lucid Gravity Robotaxi is a purpose-built autonomous ride-hailing vehicle developed by Lucid, Nuro and Uber. It is based on Lucid’s all-electric Gravity SUV and uses the Nuro Driver with a 360-degree sensor array of high-resolution cameras, lidar and radars integrated into the body and a roof-mounted Halo module. NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor provides real-time AI compute; a Halo LED display shows passenger initials and trip status, and interactive screens control seats, climate and music. The layout fits up to six passengers with luggage space. Nuro, Lucid and Uber announced autonomous on-road testing at CES 2026, a 2026 launch in a major U.S. city and Houston service in 2027; they plan 20,000 or more vehicles and cite up to 450 miles of range. No numeric price, mass, dimensions, battery endurance, runtime, speed, IP rating or navigation accuracy is published.

item.title: AGIBOT G2 Air
item.description: G2 Air is a compact single-arm mobile manipulator announced April 17, 2026 for light-duty human-in-the-loop operations. The manufacturer release lists seven manipulator DOF, three-kilogram payload, 750–800 mm reach, width under 800 mm and speeds of at least 1.5 m/s. A UMI-isomorphic layout combines task execution with data capture. The proposed transition from assisted work to full autonomy is a roadmap, not proof of unsupervised operation.

item.title: Bear Robotics Servi Q
item.description: Servi Q is specified for 45 cm / 18-inch aisles and can reverse when there is no room to turn; backward bump detection is explicitly described. The table gives 45 kg robot mass, 30 kg total payload, 10 kg per tray and 10 kg bottom shelf, with two trays plus one bottom shelf. Adjustable one-, two- or three-tray layouts are configuration options, not additional robot models.

item.title: Bear Robotics Carti 400
item.description: Carti 400 is an explicitly named low-profile configuration with 400 kg maximum cargo and 90 kg robot mass. No mass or dimensions are copied from a neighboring payload configuration. General SLAM navigation accuracy is ±10 mm; QR-code docking accuracy is ±5 mm. Marker-assisted docking is not general unmarked localization accuracy.

item.title: Bear Robotics Carti 600
item.description: Carti 600 is an explicitly named low-profile configuration with 600 kg maximum cargo and 110 kg robot mass. No mass or dimensions are copied from a neighboring payload configuration. General SLAM navigation accuracy is ±10 mm; QR-code docking accuracy is ±5 mm. Marker-assisted docking is not general unmarked localization accuracy.

item.title: Bear Robotics Carti 1000
item.description: Carti 1000 is an explicitly named low-profile configuration with 1000 kg maximum cargo and 190 kg robot mass. No mass or dimensions are copied from a neighboring payload configuration. General SLAM navigation accuracy is ±10 mm; QR-code docking accuracy is ±5 mm. Marker-assisted docking is not general unmarked localization accuracy.

item.title: Bear Robotics Carti 1500
item.description: Carti 1500 is an explicitly named low-profile configuration with 1500 kg maximum cargo and 200 kg robot mass. No mass or dimensions are copied from a neighboring payload configuration. General SLAM navigation accuracy is ±10 mm; QR-code docking accuracy is ±5 mm. Marker-assisted docking is not general unmarked localization accuracy.

item.title: Simbe Robotics Tally 4.0
item.description: Tally 4.0 is the next-generation retail inventory robot publicly launched in Simbe’s January 12, 2026 manufacturer release. That release planned customer availability beginning mid-2026; the current family page names 4.0, without proving a present transaction or stock level. Announced capabilities include up to 12 h operation per charge, ultra-high-resolution and specialty cameras, enhanced 3D depth, dual fisheye 360° sensing and NVIDIA edge computing. Faster charging has no exact elapsed duration in the selected text. No exact 4.0 mass, dimensions, payload, ingress rating or retail price is established.

item.title: Wandercraft Eve
item.description: Eve is Wandercraft's self-balancing personal exoskeleton for adults with spinal cord injury. It walks hands-free, without crutches, using 12 motors. It is FDA-cleared, available by prescription and used with a trained companion. It went on sale in the US on 17 September 2026, with other regions to follow.

item.title: Amazon Ring Rover Cam
item.description: Ring Rover Cam is Ring's autonomous indoor security robot for businesses, announced on 10 November 2026. Its AI Pilot system maps the premises, suggests patrol points and navigates around obstacles on its own. An adjustable periscope mast camera streams and records video at up to 4K. It also has a built-in siren and light tower, two-way audio and continuous person-motion detection. Sleep Mode retracts the periscope and mutes the microphone. Scheduled patrols require a compatible Ring Protect plan. US preorders open on 16 December 2026 at 999.99 USD. Amazon publishes no battery life, speed, mass, dimensions or drive details.

item.title: DJI Agras T55
item.description: Agricultural drone from DJI for high-flow spraying, spreading and lifting/transport work, with an onboard battery heat sink to keep performance stable in high temperatures. It weighs 45 kg with battery in its standard two-nozzle, 50 L tank configuration; launched globally in 2026.

item.title: DJI T200
item.description: China-market heavy-lift agricultural drone from DJI rated for payloads of up to 200 kg, with support for up to four batteries and two-aircraft coordinated lifting of up to 360 kg. Launched in April 2026 with kits priced from 99,999 CNY.

item.title: DJI FlyCart 200
item.description: China-market heavy-lift logistics drone from DJI with a 200 kg payload, support for up to four batteries and dual- or quad-aircraft coordinated lifting. It shares its airframe with the DJI T200 and was launched in April 2026.

item.title: DJI EV50
item.description: DJI's first eVTOL cargo drone, a lift-and-cruise design that takes off vertically and transitions to fixed-wing flight, with a claimed 50 kg (110 lb) payload and 150 km (93 mi) maximum range. Unveiled in July 2026 after high-altitude test flights at Mount Everest that reached 8,861 m.

item.title: Yuefan Innovation Lubao PRO
item.description: Indoor-outdoor delivery robot from Chengdu Yuefan Innovation Technology, first shown at WRC 2026, that unloads parcels by itself at each door and confirms delivery by scanning the household barcode. It handles food, express parcels and emergency supplies and integrates with gates, elevators and access-control systems; Yuefan's delivery robots operate in thousands of buildings in China.

item.title: Boston Dynamics Stretch Gen 2
item.description: Stretch Gen 2 is the second generation of Boston Dynamics' autonomous mobile trailer-unloading robot, unveiled on November 3, 2026. It adds automotive-grade connectors, an upgraded vacuum gripper, continuous-rotation joints, 81% less internal cabling and faster serviceability, unloads up to 1,000 cases per hour with multipick, runs two shifts per battery and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.

item.title: CSJBot Special Forces T1
item.description: Special Forces T1 (Tezhongbing T1) is a security patrol robot from CSJBot (Pangolin Robot) with a telescopic camera mast adjustable from 1350 to 1750 mm, a 360-degree PTZ camera, panoramic cameras, infrared night vision and 60 m lidar. It patrols indoors and outdoors on a four-wheel differential chassis, is rated IP54 and recharges automatically.

item.title: Yunji Technology Single-Arm Collaborative Robot
item.description: Yunji Technology's embodied-AI single-arm collaborative robot is a mobile manipulator for hotels, launched in July 2026 and used for tasks such as running hotel laundry rooms. It has a lifting body adjustable from 38 to 78 cm, a six-axis arm with 110 cm reach, vision sensors on the body, base and wrist, an onboard NVIDIA Orin computer and swappable grippers for cleaning, sorting and delivery tasks.

item.title: Reeman Waterproof Ant
item.description: The Waterproof Ant is a 2-ton autonomous pallet forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, launched in October 2026 for moving pallets between factory buildings over open roads in rain. It has a whole-vehicle waterproof design, a top-mounted 48-channel lidar (IP67-tested, 150 m range), laser SLAM navigation, 3D-vision pallet recognition and automatic charging; Reeman quotes a reference price of about USD 14,000.

item.title: Reeman YIMA Outdoor Delivery Robot (YBOT20P)
item.description: YIMA (YBOT20P) is an outdoor material-delivery robot from Shenzhen Reeman for factory roads, warehouses, connected buildings and residential parcel delivery. It carries 100 kg, navigates with dual-laser SLAM (360-degree top lidar up to 100 m plus a 230-degree front lidar), climbs 10% grades, runs 10-15 hours and can integrate with elevators and automatic doors; it is specified for dry paved roads, not rain.

item.title: Geely 7 kW Underbody AGV Charging Robot
item.description: Geely's 7 kW underbody AGV charging robot is an automatic EV charging robot unveiled at the Geely AI Smart Charging launch in September 2026 for residential communities and private parking spaces. The low-profile AGV drives under a parked car, aligns automatically with an underbody charging port and charges overnight; Geely said its three charging robots would launch in the near term.

item.title: Geely 20 kW Automatic Charging Robot
item.description: Geely's 20 kW automatic charging robot is a compact robotic EV charger unveiled in September 2026 for shopping districts, office parks and public car parks with medium dwell times. It automates plug-in charging without driver involvement while limiting the load added to the local commercial power grid; it is one of three automatic charging robots Geely announced alongside its AI Smart Charging technology.

item.title: Geely 1.5 MW Ultra-Fast Charging Robot
item.description: Geely's 1.5 MW ultra-fast charging robot is a robotic-arm megawatt EV charger unveiled in September 2026 for expressway service areas. A fully automatic arm with multimodal perception locates the charging port and connects the heavy liquid-cooled cable so drivers need not leave the car; it is the top model of the three automatic charging robots Geely announced.

item.title: Saite Intelligence Jingjie S1
item.description: Jingjie S1 is a compact autonomous outdoor sweeping robot from Guangzhou Saite Intelligence, launched on April 1, 2026 at 99,000 CNY (or 2,999 CNY per month rental) for residential estates, campuses and business parks. It plans routes and avoids obstacles with a 16-line lidar, automatically bags and drops collected waste, sprays water to suppress dust, sweeps up to 1350 mm wide at over 4,700 m² per hour and refills and recharges automatically.

item.title: Excelland (UDI) Youxiaomei M7
item.description: Youxiaomei M7 is the seventh-generation hotel and office-building delivery robot from Shenzhen-based UDI (Excelland Robotics), launched at the 2026 Shanghai hotel expo on March 31, 2026. A movable divider switches it between two compartments (30 L + 25 L) and one 50 L compartment, it charges wirelessly, and upward- and downward-facing RGBD cameras provide stereo obstacle avoidance; it passes 62 cm corridors.

item.title: Excelland (UDI) Youxiaomei MX
item.description: Youxiaomei MX is an embodied-AI indoor delivery robot from UDI (Excelland Robotics), launched on March 31, 2026 at the Meadin hotel development forum in Shanghai. A six-axis arm with gripper and 626 mm reach presses elevator buttons between 70 and 140 cm, so it rides elevators without IoT retrofits, and it can hand over items or knock on doors; it carries 10 kg in a 28 L compartment and navigates with fused VSLAM and laser SLAM.

item.title: Cainiao ZeeBot
item.description: Cainiao's self-developed climbing robot is a rack-climbing bin-retrieval robot for automated warehouses, launched in April 2026 and upgraded at CeMAT Asia in November 2026. It climbs onto racks and retrieves totes from four sides, supports double-deep storage, and is used in cross-border e-commerce, fashion, electronics, FMCG, healthcare and automotive warehouses, with an international version for EU and US standards.

item.title: Reeman Hussar Pro
item.description: Hussar Pro is a factory and warehouse delivery robot from Shenzhen Reeman for frequent in-plant transport of parts, tools, bins and work-in-progress. It carries 80 kg, positions and avoids obstacles with lidar plus a 3D vision system, runs on a lithium iron phosphate battery with automatic return to its charger, and supports remote scheduling and route planning.

item.title: Zelos (Jiushi) Z10 Pro
item.description: The Z10 Pro is a 2.5-ton heavy-load L4 driverless urban logistics van from Zelos (Jiushi Intelligent), launched at the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September 2026. Zelos lists a 2,500 kg payload, 12.5 m³ cargo box, 55.91 kWh battery and up to 300 km unladen range; a refrigerated Z10 Pro variant is also offered.

item.title: Reeman X-ant Autonomous Forklift
item.description: X-ant is a 2-ton autonomous pallet forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, launched in April 2026 for narrow-aisle warehouses and factories up to 40,000 m² with EU and US pallets. It has 550 mm fork width, a 1448 mm turning radius, PLC plus industrial-PC control, marker-free laser SLAM navigation, and solid-state TOF lidar, multi-line lidar and 3D vision for 360-degree obstacle detection up to 50 m.

item.title: Blueye Robotics X7
item.description: The Blueye X7 is an inspection-class underwater ROV from Norway's Blueye Robotics with seven thrusters, seven guest ports for payloads such as manipulators and sonars, a 4K camera and an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX for AI processing. It is rated to 500 m depth, weighs 20 kg in air and runs on dual batteries or optional topside power; it was launched in May 2026 as the company's new flagship.

item.title: Blueye Robotics X3 Ultra
item.description: The Blueye X3 Ultra is an upgraded portable mini-ROV from Blueye Robotics with a 4K HDR camera, onboard Jetson Orin NX AI processing, a new IMU and three guest ports for external equipment. It is rated to 305 m, moves at 1.5 m/s and weighs 8.6 kg; it was launched in May 2026 alongside the X7.

item.title: Brokk 110+
item.description: The Brokk 110+ is a compact electric, remote-controlled demolition robot from Swedish maker Brokk, launched in January 2026 as the SmartPower+ successor to the Brokk 110. It weighs 990 kg, delivers 19.5 kW, fits in elevators and on car trailers, and reaches 4.3 m vertically with a breaker.

item.title: Johnson & Johnson MedTech OTTAVA
item.description: OTTAVA is a soft-tissue robotic surgical system from Johnson & Johnson MedTech whose four robotic arms are integrated into the operating-room table, which the company says takes 30-50% less space than boom- and cart-mounted systems and supports synchronized table-and-arm motion. It received FDA De Novo marketing authorization on July 22, 2026 for upper-abdominal and general procedures including gastric bypass, gastrectomy, cholecystectomy and hiatal hernia repair.

item.title: Berkshire Grey Scoop
item.description: Scoop is a robotic trailer and container unloader from Berkshire Grey that combines selective picking and pulling with conveyor-enabled floor induction to bulk-unload structured, unstructured and floor-loaded parcels, with a manual mode for non-conveyable exceptions. It was launched on February 3, 2026, when FedEx announced deployment of the system during 2026 after a multi-year collaboration.

item.title: Naïo Technologies SANKA
item.description: Fully electric autonomous tracked tool carrier from Naïo Technologies for vineyards, orchards and other perennial crops, offered in Compact (1.3 m) and Large (1.8 m) versions with a 3-point hitch, PTO, auxiliary hydraulics and an on-board power supply for existing implements. It uses a patented dynamic mass-balancing system, human- and obstacle-detection sensors and geofencing; unveiled in November 2026 and winner of an EIMA 2026 award, it is available for pre-order with delivery in 2027.

item.title: Wingcopter 262
item.description: The Wingcopter 262 is a modular all-electric VTOL reconnaissance drone from German maker Wingcopter, named after its 262 cm wingspan and aimed at defence and security users. It carries AI-enabled EO/IR camera systems, has a 10 kg maximum take-off weight, a 150 km tactical range and up to six hours of flight time; it was introduced in September 2026.

item.title: Geek+ RoboShuttle Hyper
item.description: Tote-to-person rack-climbing robot system from Geek+ that delivers up to 6,000 totes per hour per 1,000 m², climbs at up to 1.5 m/s and allows two robots to work in the same rack column. Its Max Workstation exceeds 800 totes per hour; launched in August 2026 alongside the existing RoboShuttle Air and Flex.

item.title: United Imaging uSurg DoctorX
item.description: Multi-arm laparoscopic/endoscopic surgical robot developed by Wuhan United Imaging Zhirong Medical Technology, a surgical-innovation subsidiary of United Imaging Healthcare. Clinically validated in hepatobiliary, urologic, gastrointestinal, gynecologic and thoracic procedures at top Chinese hospitals, and approved by China's NMPA on 30 July 2026 as the group's first laparoscopic/endoscopic surgical robot.

item.title: Multiway Robotics OT10
item.description: Omnidirectional autonomous pallet truck from Multiway Robotics with a 1,000 kg rated load, 1.7 m/s top speed and 360° movement that allows right-angle stacking in 1,900 mm aisles. It uses 3D SLAM navigation without reflectors or QR codes and can ride elevators between floors; launched in June 2026 and winner of a 2026 French Design Award.

item.title: Hikrobot Z1-300
item.description: Latent (under-ride) transport AMR in Hikrobot's Mingzhi single-unit intelligence series, carrying 300 kg for line-side material delivery without a central server; deployment can take as little as 30 minutes. It passes aisles as narrow as 60 cm and was launched on 23 October 2026.

item.title: Hikrobot Z2-1500
item.description: Fork-type transport AMR in Hikrobot's Mingzhi series with a 1,500 kg load capacity for pallet transport and stacking, supporting walk-through teaching of routes and server-free multi-robot coordination. Launched on 23 October 2026.

item.title: Standard Robots EasyGo
item.description: Lightweight indoor delivery AMR from Standard Robots with a 150 kg rated load, about 12 hours of runtime unloaded (8 hours loaded) and automatic recharging. It maps about 1,000 m² in 10 minutes, passes 550 mm gaps and uses dual LiDAR plus cameras; launched on 10 October 2026.

item.title: Jiexiang Lingyue FK-80
item.description: Fork-type autonomous mobile robot from Jiexiang Lingyue whose maximum lift height was raised from 6.5 m to 8 m while keeping a 1.2 t load capacity over the full stroke, for higher pallet storage locations. Launched on 15 October 2026.

item.title: Dolphin Star ML03
item.description: Compact line-side transport AMR nicknamed 'Little Turtle' from Dolphin Star, with a 920 x 400 mm body and 690 mm minimum turning radius for narrow-aisle material handling. Shown publicly for the first time in October 2026.
